packs.name: 7-Zip archive
packs.description: 7z signature header: version, CRCs, and the pointer to the (usually compressed) end header.
packs.author: Nybble

formats.name: 7Z
formats.schema:
// 7-Zip (.7z) — a 32-byte signature header at the start of the file, the
// packed streams, and then the real header at the very end. The start header
// only tells you where that end header is; everything else (file names, sizes,
// coders) lives in the end header, and 7-Zip almost always LZMA-compresses it
// (property id 0x17 = EncodedHeader), so it is shown here as raw bytes with
// its leading property id decoded.

enum SevenZipProperty : u8 {
    End                   = 0x00
    Header                = 0x01
    ArchiveProperties     = 0x02
    AdditionalStreamsInfo = 0x03
    MainStreamsInfo       = 0x04
    FilesInfo             = 0x05
    PackInfo              = 0x06
    UnPackInfo            = 0x07
    SubStreamsInfo        = 0x08
    Size                  = 0x09
    Crc                   = 0x0A
    Folder                = 0x0B
    CodersUnPackSize      = 0x0C
    NumUnPackStream       = 0x0D
    EmptyStream           = 0x0E
    EmptyFile             = 0x0F
    Anti                  = 0x10
    Name                  = 0x11
    CTime                 = 0x12
    ATime                 = 0x13
    MTime                 = 0x14
    WinAttributes         = 0x15
    Comment               = 0x16
    EncodedHeader         = 0x17
    StartPos              = 0x18
    Dummy                 = 0x19
}

struct SevenZip {
    signature        bytes[6] "37 7A BC AF 27 1C"
    versionMajor     u8       "format major version (0)"
    versionMinor     u8       "format minor version (2..4)"
    startHeaderCrc   u32      "CRC-32 of the next 20 bytes"
    nextHeaderOffset u64      "end header position, relative to the end of this 32-byte header"
    nextHeaderSize   u64      "end header size in bytes"
    nextHeaderCrc    u32      "CRC-32 of the end header"
    nextHeaderPos    = nextHeaderOffset + 32
    // The packed streams occupy bytes 32 .. nextHeaderPos.
    nextHeaderKind at nextHeaderPos SevenZipProperty      if nextHeaderSize > 0 "0x01 = plain header, 0x17 = compressed (encoded) header"
    nextHeader     at nextHeaderPos bytes[nextHeaderSize] if nextHeaderSize > 0 "the end header (7z property stream)"
}

packs.description: Apple File System container superblock, its object map, and the first volume superblock it maps to.
packs.author: Nybble

formats.name: APFS
formats.description: APFS container (NXSB), as a raw partition or image
formats.schema:
// APFS - the Apple File System, on every Mac, iPhone and iPad since 2017. A
// partition holds one container; the container holds any number of volumes
// sharing its free space (Macintosh HD and Macintosh HD - Data, Preboot,
// Recovery, VM). Point this at the APFS partition itself, not at a whole disk:
// in a full-disk image the container starts after the GPT.
//
// Everything is an object in fixed-size blocks (4096 bytes in practice) with
// a common 32-byte header: a Fletcher-64 checksum, an object id, the
// transaction id that wrote it, and a type. Physical objects are addressed by
// block number; virtual ones (like volume superblocks) by an id that the
// container's object map translates to a block.
//
// Block 0 holds a copy of the container superblock made at the last
// checkpoint. A mounted container's newest one lives in the checkpoint
// descriptor area; block 0 is what a reader starts from to find it.
//
// The object map is followed one step here: its B-tree root (when it is a
// single leaf, as on any small container) gives the block of the first volume
// superblock. That step assumes 4096-byte blocks.

bitfield ApfsObjectType : u32 {
    type          0..15 // 1 container superblock, 2 B-tree root, 3 B-tree node, 11 object map, 13 volume superblock
    nonpersistent 27
    encrypted     28
    noHeader      29
    physical      30 // addressed by block number
    ephemeral     31 // lives only in the checkpoint area
}

bitfield ApfsContainerFeatures : u64 {
    defrag             0
    lowCapacityFusion  1 // a Fusion drive with a small SSD tier
}

bitfield ApfsIncompatibleFeatures : u64 {
    version1 0 // the pre-release macOS 10.12 format
    version2 1 // APFS as shipped
    fusion   8 // a Fusion drive container
}

bitfield ApfsVolumeIncompatibleFeatures : u64 {
    caseInsensitive        0
    datalessSnapshots      1
    encryptionRolled       2
    normalizationInsensitive 3
    incompleteRestore      4
    sealedVolume           5
}

enum ApfsVolumeRole : u16 {
    None       = 0
    System     = 1
    User       = 2
    Recovery   = 4
    Vm         = 8
    Preboot    = 16
    Installer  = 32
    Data       = 64
    Baseband   = 128
    Update     = 192
    Xart       = 256
    Hardware   = 320
    Backup     = 384
    Enterprise = 576
    Prelogin   = 704
}

struct ApfsObjectHeader {
    checksum u64            "Fletcher-64 over the rest of the block"
    oid      u64            "object id: a block number for physical objects"
    xid      u64            "transaction that last wrote this object"
    type     ApfsObjectType
    subtype  u32            "for a B-tree, what it indexes (11 object map, 14 filesystem records)"
}

struct ApfsPrange {
    start u64 "first block"
    count u64 "number of blocks"
}

struct ApfsModifiedBy {
    id        string[32] "the software that did it, e.g. a newfs_apfs or apfsd version"
    timestamp u64        "nanoseconds since 1970"
    lastXid   u64        "last transaction it wrote"
}

// Volume superblock: one per volume, found through the object map.
struct ApfsVolume {
    header                  ApfsObjectHeader
    magic                   char[4]  "APSB"
    fsIndex                 u32      "this volume's slot in the container's volume list"
    features                u64      "bit 0 legacy defrag, bit 1 hard-link maps, bit 2 defrag"
    readonlyCompatibleFeatures u64
    incompatibleFeatures    ApfsVolumeIncompatibleFeatures
    unmountTime             u64      "nanoseconds since 1970"
    reserveBlockCount       u64      "blocks guaranteed to this volume"
    quotaBlockCount         u64      "the most blocks this volume may use, 0 for no limit"
    allocCount              u64      "blocks in use"
    metaCrypto              bytes[20] "how the volume's metadata is protected"
    rootTreeType            u32
    extentrefTreeType       u32
    snapMetaTreeType        u32
    omapOid                 u64      "block of this volume's own object map"
    rootTreeOid             u64      "virtual id of the filesystem tree: inodes, directory entries, extents"
    extentrefTreeOid        u64
    snapMetaTreeOid         u64
    revertToXid             u64
    revertToSblockOid       u64
    nextObjId               u64      "next inode number to hand out"
    numFiles                u64
    numDirectories          u64
    numSymlinks             u64
    numOtherFsObjects       u64
    numSnapshots            u64
    totalBlocksAlloced      u64
    totalBlocksFreed        u64
    volumeUuid              bytes[16]
    lastModTime             u64      "nanoseconds since 1970"
    fsFlags                 u64      "bit 0 unencrypted, bit 3 one key, bit 4 spilled over"
    formattedBy             ApfsModifiedBy "who created the volume"
    modifiedBy              ApfsModifiedBy[8] "the last eight to mount it for writing, newest first"
    volumeName              string[256] "volume name, UTF-8"
    nextDocId               u32
    role                    ApfsVolumeRole "what the volume is for"
}

struct ApfsOmapMapping {
    oid   u64 "virtual object id"
    xid   u64 "transaction of this version"
}

struct ApfsOmapValue {
    flags u32 "bit 0 deleted, bit 2 encrypted"
    size  u32 "object size in bytes"
    paddr u64 "block holding the object"
    volumeAt = paddr * 4096
    volume at volumeAt ApfsVolume "the object, read as a volume superblock"
}

// Root of the object map's B-tree. Entries have fixed-size keys and values,
// located through a table of contents of (key, value) offset pairs: keys count
// up from after the table, values down from the end of the block, before the
// 40-byte B-tree info a root node carries. The table is read right after the
// header, since its offset is always 0 in practice.
struct ApfsOmapRoot {
    header      ApfsObjectHeader
    flags       u16 "bit 0 root, bit 1 leaf, bit 2 fixed-size keys and values"
    level       u16 "0 for a leaf"
    keyCount    u32 "entries in this node"
    tableOffset u16 "table of contents, from the end of this header"
    tableLength u16
    freeOffset  u16
    freeLength  u16
    keyFreeList u32
    valueFreeList u32
    firstKeyOffset   u16 "offset of the first key, from the end of the table"
    firstValueOffset u16 "offset of the first value, back from the B-tree info"
    keyAt   = 56 + tableOffset + tableLength + firstKeyOffset
    valueAt = 4096 - 40 - firstValueOffset
    firstKey   at +keyAt   ApfsOmapMapping "first mapping: which object"
    firstValue at +valueAt ApfsOmapValue   if level == 0 "first mapping: where it is"
}

struct ApfsOmap {
    header             ApfsObjectHeader
    flags              u32 "bit 0 manually managed, bit 1 encrypting, bit 2 decrypting"
    snapshotCount      u32
    treeType           u32
    snapshotTreeType   u32
    treeOid            u64 "block of the B-tree root"
    snapshotTreeOid    u64
    mostRecentSnapshot u64
    pendingRevertMin   u64
    pendingRevertMax   u64
}

struct Apfs {
    header                 ApfsObjectHeader
    magic                  char[4]  "NXSB"
    blockSize              u32      "bytes per block, 4096"
    blockCount             u64      "blocks in the container"
    features               ApfsContainerFeatures
    readonlyCompatibleFeatures u64
    incompatibleFeatures   ApfsIncompatibleFeatures
    uuid                   bytes[16] "container UUID"
    nextOid                u64      "next object id to hand out"
    nextXid                u64      "next transaction id"
    xpDescBlocks           u32      "checkpoint descriptor area size; top bit set if it is not contiguous"
    xpDataBlocks           u32      "checkpoint data area size"
    xpDescBase             u64      "first block of the checkpoint descriptor area"
    xpDataBase             u64      "first block of the checkpoint data area"
    xpDescNext             u32
    xpDataNext             u32
    xpDescIndex            u32      "where the newest checkpoint starts in the descriptor area"
    xpDescLen              u32
    xpDataIndex            u32
    xpDataLen              u32
    spacemanOid            u64      "space manager, an ephemeral object"
    omapOid                u64      "block of the container's object map"
    reaperOid              u64
    testType               u32
    maxFileSystems         u32      "how many volumes the container can hold"
    fsOid                  u64[100] "virtual id of each volume's superblock, 0 for an empty slot"
    counters               u64[32]
    blockedOutRange        ApfsPrange "blocks being evacuated by a resize"
    evictMappingTreeOid    u64
    flags                  u64      "bit 1 software crypto"
    efiJumpstart           u64      "block of the EFI driver record, what lets firmware boot from APFS"
    fusionUuid             bytes[16]
    keylocker              ApfsPrange "the container keybag"
    ephemeralInfo          u64[4]
    testOid                u64
    fusionMtOid            u64
    fusionWbcOid           u64
    fusionWbc              ApfsPrange
    newestMountedVersion   u64
    mkbLocker              ApfsPrange
    omapAt = omapOid * blockSize
    omap at omapAt ApfsOmap "the container's object map: virtual id to block"
    omapTreeAt = omap.treeOid * blockSize
    omapTree at omapTreeAt ApfsOmapRoot "its B-tree root"
}

formats.name: DDS
formats.description: DirectDraw Surface texture: the 124-byte header, its pixel format, and the DX10 extension.
formats.schema:
// DDS (DirectDraw Surface) — little-endian. A four-byte magic, a fixed 124-byte
// DDS_HEADER with a nested DDS_PIXELFORMAT, then the surface data. When the
// pixel format's FourCC is 'DX10' a second, 20-byte header precedes that data.

// Which DDS_HEADER fields carry a meaningful value. Caps, height, width,
// pixelFormat are required; the rest describe what the file happens to hold.
bitfield DdsHeaderFlags : u32 {
    caps        0  // required
    height      1  // required
    width       2  // required
    pitch       3  // pitchOrLinearSize holds a row pitch (uncompressed)
    pixelFormat 12 // required
    mipMapCount 17 // the file stores a mipmap chain
    linearSize  19 // pitchOrLinearSize holds a total size (block compressed)
    depth       23 // the surface is a volume texture
}

bitfield DdsPixelFormatFlags : u32 {
    alphaPixels 0  // the surface has per-pixel alpha, described by aBitMask
    alpha       1  // alpha-only surface: rgbBitCount and aBitMask apply
    fourCC      2  // compressed: the encoding is named by fourCC
    rgb         6  // uncompressed RGB: the channel masks apply
    yuv         9  // uncompressed YUV, packed in the RGB masks
    luminance   17 // single-channel luminance, in rBitMask
}

bitfield DdsCaps : u32 {
    complex 3  // the file holds more than one surface (mipmaps, cube, volume)
    texture 12 // required on every DDS file
    mipmap  22 // this surface is part of a mipmap chain
}

bitfield DdsCaps2 : u32 {
    cubemap          9  // the file is a cube map
    cubemapPositiveX 10
    cubemapNegativeX 11
    cubemapPositiveY 12
    cubemapNegativeY 13
    cubemapPositiveZ 14
    cubemapNegativeZ 15
    volume           21 // the file is a volume (3D) texture
}

// The DXGI formats a DX10-extended DDS commonly carries; the full enumeration
// runs past 130 entries.
enum DxgiFormat : u32 {
    Unknown           = 0
    R32G32B32A32Float = 2
    R16G16B16A16Float = 10
    R8G8B8A8Unorm     = 28
    R8G8B8A8UnormSrgb = 29
    R16Float          = 54
    R8Unorm           = 61
    Bc1Unorm          = 71
    Bc1UnormSrgb      = 72
    Bc2Unorm          = 74
    Bc2UnormSrgb      = 75
    Bc3Unorm          = 77
    Bc3UnormSrgb      = 78
    Bc4Unorm          = 80
    Bc5Unorm          = 83
    B8G8R8A8Unorm     = 87
    B8G8R8A8UnormSrgb = 91
    Bc6hUf16          = 95
    Bc7Unorm          = 98
    Bc7UnormSrgb      = 99
}

enum DdsResourceDimension : u32 {
    Texture1D = 2
    Texture2D = 3
    Texture3D = 4
}

// The DX10 extension header, present only when fourCC is 'DX10'.
struct DdsHeaderDxt10 {
    dxgiFormat        DxgiFormat           "the surface format, in DXGI terms"
    resourceDimension DdsResourceDimension "1D, 2D or 3D resource"
    miscFlag          u32                  "bit 2 marks a cube map"
    arraySize         u32                  "number of elements in the texture array"
    miscFlags2        u32                  "alpha mode: 0 unknown, 1 straight, 2 premultiplied, 3 opaque"
}

struct DdsPixelFormat {
    size        u32                  "size of this block in bytes, always 32"
    flags       DdsPixelFormatFlags  "which of the fields below are meaningful"
    fourCC      char[4]              "compression FourCC (DXT1..DXT5, DX10, ATI2, ...) when the fourCC flag is set"
    rgbBitCount u32                  "bits per pixel for an uncompressed surface"
    rBitMask    u32                  "red channel mask"
    gBitMask    u32                  "green channel mask"
    bBitMask    u32                  "blue channel mask"
    aBitMask    u32                  "alpha channel mask"
    // The DX10 header sits just past the 124-byte DDS_HEADER. This block starts
    // at file offset 76, so that is +52 from here. Placed by pointer, so it
    // reads no bytes of its own and the fixed header layout stays exact.
    dx10 at +52 match fourCC {
        "DX10"  => DdsHeaderDxt10
        default => bytes[0]
    }
}

struct Dds {
    magic             char[4]        "magic 'DDS '"
    size              u32            "size of the header that follows, always 124"
    flags             DdsHeaderFlags "which header fields carry a meaningful value"
    height            u32            "surface height in pixels"
    width             u32            "surface width in pixels"
    pitchOrLinearSize u32            "row pitch, or the total size of the top-level surface"
    depth             u32            "depth of a volume texture, in pixels"
    mipMapCount       u32            "number of mipmap levels"
    reserved1         bytes[44]      "reserved; some tools stash a writer signature here"
    pixelFormat       DdsPixelFormat "how each pixel is encoded"
    caps              DdsCaps        "surface complexity flags"
    caps2             DdsCaps2       "cube map and volume texture flags"
    caps3             u32            "unused, zero"
    caps4             u32            "unused, zero"
    reserved2         u32            "reserved, zero"
    surface           bytes[*]       "the surface data: mip chain, cube faces or volume slices"
}

formats.name: ELF
formats.description: ELF executable, shared object or core dump (little-endian)
formats.schema:
// ELF - the Unix executable, shared object and core dump container. The first
// sixteen bytes (e_ident) are byte-order and width independent on purpose: they
// say what the rest of the file is before anything else is read. Everything
// after them changes width with the class, so the wide fields appear twice
// below, each guarded by ident.class; only one set is ever present.
//
// A file carries two views of the same bytes. The program headers are the
// loader's view, a list of chunks to map and where to map them. The section
// headers are the linker's view: .text, .data, .symtab and friends. Both
// tables are followed here from the offsets in the header, by pointer, so the
// header itself stays exactly ehsize bytes long.

enum ElfClass : u8 {
    NoClass = 0
    Elf32   = 1
    Elf64   = 2
}

enum ElfData : u8 {
    NoData       = 0
    LittleEndian = 1
    BigEndian    = 2
}

enum ElfOsAbi : u8 {
    SystemV    = 0
    HpUx       = 1
    NetBsd     = 2
    Linux      = 3
    Solaris    = 6
    Aix        = 7
    Irix       = 8
    FreeBsd    = 9
    OpenBsd    = 12
    ArmAeabi   = 64
    Arm        = 97
    Standalone = 255
}

enum ElfType : u16 {
    NoType = 0
    Rel    = 1
    Exec   = 2
    Dyn    = 3
    Core   = 4
}

enum ElfMachine : u16 {
    NoMachine = 0
    Sparc     = 2
    I386      = 3
    M68k      = 4
    Mips      = 8
    PowerPc   = 20
    PowerPc64 = 21
    S390      = 22
    Arm       = 40
    SuperH    = 42
    SparcV9   = 43
    Ia64      = 50
    X86_64    = 62
    Aarch64   = 183
    RiscV     = 243
    Bpf       = 247
    LoongArch = 258
}

enum ElfSegmentType : u32 {
    Null        = 0
    Load        = 1
    Dynamic     = 2
    Interp      = 3
    Note        = 4
    Shlib       = 5
    Phdr        = 6
    Tls         = 7
    GnuEhFrame  = 0x6474E550
    GnuStack    = 0x6474E551
    GnuRelro    = 0x6474E552
    GnuProperty = 0x6474E553
}

enum ElfSectionType : u32 {
    Null          = 0
    Progbits      = 1
    Symtab        = 2
    Strtab        = 3
    Rela          = 4
    Hash          = 5
    Dynamic       = 6
    Note          = 7
    Nobits        = 8
    Rel           = 9
    Shlib         = 10
    Dynsym        = 11
    InitArray     = 14
    FiniArray     = 15
    PreinitArray  = 16
    Group         = 17
    SymtabShndx   = 18
    GnuAttributes = 0x6FFFFFF5
    GnuHash       = 0x6FFFFFF6
    GnuVerdef     = 0x6FFFFFFD
    GnuVerneed    = 0x6FFFFFFE
    GnuVersym     = 0x6FFFFFFF
}

bitfield ElfSegmentFlags : u32 {
    execute 0
    write   1
    read    2
}

bitfield ElfSectionFlags : u32 {
    write           0  // writable at run time
    alloc           1  // occupies memory in the loaded image
    execinstr       2  // executable machine instructions
    merge           4  // may be merged to remove duplicates
    strings         5  // holds NUL-terminated strings
    infoLink        6  // info holds a section header index
    linkOrder       7  // ordering constraints on linking
    osNonconforming 8
    group           9  // member of a section group
    tls             10 // thread-local storage
    compressed      11 // contents are compressed, prefixed by a compression header
}

// e_ident - the sixteen bytes every ELF reader parses before anything else.
struct ElfIdent {
    magic      bytes[4] "7F 45 4C 46, the ELF magic"
    class      ElfClass "32- or 64-bit; sets the width of every offset below"

    machine   ElfMachine "target architecture"

// FAT32 boot sector - the same BPB as FAT16 for the first 36 bytes, then a
// different tail. The changes are all about size: the table length becomes
// 32-bit, and the root directory stops being a fixed area at a fixed place and
// becomes an ordinary cluster chain, so the sector has to say which cluster it
// starts at. rootEntries and sectorsPerFat16 are left as zero to make an old
// driver refuse the volume rather than misread it.
//
// FAT32 also adds two backup structures: a copy of this sector, usually at
// sector 6, and an FS information sector holding a cached free-cluster count.

enum FatMediaDescriptor : u8 {
    Floppy144M = 0xF0
    FixedDisk  = 0xF8
}

struct Fat32 {
    jump              bytes[3] "a short jump over the BPB to the boot code"
    oemName           char[8]  "formatting system"
    bytesPerSector    u16      "512 on essentially everything"
    sectorsPerCluster u8       "cluster size, a power of two"
    reservedSectors   u16      "sectors before the first allocation table, usually 32"
    numberOfFats      u8       "copies of the allocation table, normally 2"
    rootEntries       u16      "always 0 on FAT32: the root is a cluster chain"
    totalSectors16    u16      "always 0 on FAT32"
    mediaDescriptor   FatMediaDescriptor "media type, echoed in the first FAT entry"
    sectorsPerFat16   u16      "always 0 on FAT32; see sectorsPerFat32"
    sectorsPerTrack   u16      "disk geometry, for the BIOS"
    numberOfHeads     u16      "disk geometry, for the BIOS"
    hiddenSectors     u32      "sectors before this partition on the disk"
    totalSectors32    u32      "sectors on the volume"
    sectorsPerFat32   u32      "sectors in one allocation table"
    extFlags          u16      "bits 0-3 the active FAT, bit 7 set means only it is live"
    fsVersion         u16      "0"
    rootCluster       u32      "first cluster of the root directory, normally 2"
    fsInfoSector      u16      "sector holding the FS information structure, normally 1"
    backupBootSector  u16      "sector holding the backup boot sector, normally 6"
    reserved          bytes[12] "zero"
    driveNumber       u8       "BIOS drive: 0x80 for a hard disk"
    reserved2         u8       "reused by Windows NT as a dirty flag"
    bootSignature     u8       "0x29 when the three fields below are present"
    volumeSerial      u32      "serial number, generated at format time"
    volumeLabel       char[11] "volume label, space padded"
    fileSystemType    char[8]  "FAT32 followed by three spaces; advisory only"
    bootCode          bytes[420] "the boot code the jump above lands in"

}

formats.name: GB
formats.description: Game Boy / Game Boy Color cartridge ROM
formats.schema:
// Game Boy cartridge - the header sits at 0x100, immediately after the
// interrupt and RST vectors, because that is where the boot ROM hands control
// over. The 48 bytes after the entry point are a bitmap of the Nintendo logo:
// the boot ROM draws it and then compares it byte for byte against its own
// copy, halting on any difference. It was a trademark lock, not a checksum,
// and it is the most reliable way to recognise a Game Boy ROM.
//
// The header checksum is the other half of that lock. The boot ROM verifies it
// too, so a ROM with the wrong value will not start on real hardware. The
// global checksum over the whole cartridge is not verified and is often wrong
// in dumps and hacks.
//
// The title field shrank over time. On the original it was 16 characters; the
// Game Boy Color took the last five for the manufacturer code and the CGB
// flag, which is why titles in later games are cut to 11.

enum GbCartridgeType : u8 {
    RomOnly              = 0x00
    Mbc1                 = 0x01
    Mbc1Ram              = 0x02
    Mbc1RamBattery       = 0x03
    Mbc2                 = 0x05
    Mbc2Battery          = 0x06
    RomRam               = 0x08
    RomRamBattery        = 0x09
    Mmm01                = 0x0B
    Mmm01Ram             = 0x0C
    Mmm01RamBattery      = 0x0D
    Mbc3TimerBattery     = 0x0F
    Mbc3TimerRamBattery  = 0x10
    Mbc3                 = 0x11
    Mbc3Ram              = 0x12
    Mbc3RamBattery       = 0x13
    Mbc5                 = 0x19
    Mbc5Ram              = 0x1A
    Mbc5RamBattery       = 0x1B
    Mbc5Rumble           = 0x1C
    Mbc5RumbleRam        = 0x1D
    Mbc5RumbleRamBattery = 0x1E
    Mbc6                 = 0x20
    Mbc7SensorRumble     = 0x22
    PocketCamera         = 0xFC
    BandaiTama5          = 0xFD
    Huc3                 = 0xFE
    Huc1RamBattery       = 0xFF
}

enum GbRomSize : u8 {
    Kib32  = 0 // 2 banks, no bank switching needed
    Kib64  = 1
    Kib128 = 2
    Kib256 = 3
    Kib512 = 4
    Mib1   = 5
    Mib2   = 6
    Mib4   = 7
    Mib8   = 8

    vectors         bytes[256] "0x00-0xFF: the RST and interrupt vectors"
    entryPoint      bytes[4]   "usually nop; jp 0x0150, run after the boot ROM"

formats.name: GGUF
formats.description: GGUF model file (llama.cpp / GGML), version 2 or 3
formats.schema:
// GGUF - the single-file model format of llama.cpp and the GGML family, and
// what most locally run language models are downloaded as. Everything a
// loader needs travels in one file: a header, a list of typed metadata
// key/value pairs (architecture, context length, the tokenizer's whole
// vocabulary), a directory of tensors, then the tensor data itself.
//
// Strings are a 64-bit length followed by UTF-8 bytes, with no terminator.
// Version 1 used 32-bit counts and lengths; this pack reads versions 2 and 3,
// which is everything written since 2023.
//
// Tensor offsets are relative to the start of the data section, which begins
// at the first multiple of general.alignment (32 unless that key says
// otherwise) after the tensor directory.

enum GgufValueType : u32 {
    Uint8   = 0
    Int8    = 1
    Uint16  = 2
    Int16   = 3
    Uint32  = 4
    Int32   = 5
    Float32 = 6
    Bool    = 7
    String  = 8
    Array   = 9
    Uint64  = 10
    Int64   = 11
    Float64 = 12
}

enum GgmlType : u32 {
    F32     = 0
    F16     = 1
    Q4_0    = 2
    Q4_1    = 3
    Q5_0    = 6
    Q5_1    = 7
    Q8_0    = 8
    Q8_1    = 9
    Q2_K    = 10
    Q3_K    = 11
    Q4_K    = 12
    Q5_K    = 13
    Q6_K    = 14
    Q8_K    = 15
    IQ2_XXS = 16
    IQ2_XS  = 17
    IQ3_XXS = 18
    IQ1_S   = 19
    IQ4_NL  = 20
    IQ3_S   = 21
    IQ2_S   = 22
    IQ4_XS  = 23
    I8      = 24
    I16     = 25
    I32     = 26
    I64     = 27
    F64     = 28
    IQ1_M   = 29
    BF16    = 30
    TQ1_0   = 34
    TQ2_0   = 35
    MXFP4   = 39
}

struct GgufString {
    length u64            "bytes of UTF-8 text"
    text   string[length]
}

// An array value: an element type, a count, then the elements back to back.
// Arrays of arrays exist in the spec but no writer emits them.
struct GgufArray {
    type   GgufValueType "element type"
    count  u64           "number of elements"
    items  match type {
        0  => u8[count]
        1  => i8[count]
        2  => u16[count]
        3  => i16[count]
        4  => u32[count]
        5  => i32[count]
        6  => f32[count]
        7  => u8[count]
        8  => GgufString[count]
        10 => u64[count]
        11 => i64[count]
        12 => f64[count]
    }
}

struct GgufKv {
    key   GgufString    "dotted key, e.g. general.architecture or llama.context_length"
    type  GgufValueType "type of the value that follows"
    value match type {
        0  => u8
        1  => i8
        2  => u16
        3  => i16
        4  => u32
        5  => i32
        6  => f32
        7  => bool
        8  => GgufString
        9  => GgufArray
        10 => u64
        11 => i64
        12 => f64
    }
}

struct GgufTensorInfo {
    name   GgufString "tensor name, e.g. blk.0.attn_q.weight"
    nDims  u32        "number of dimensions, at most 4"
    dims   u64[nDims] "size of each dimension, innermost first"
    type   GgmlType   "element type or quantization scheme"
    offset u64        "offset of the tensor's data from the start of the data section"
}

struct Gguf {
    magic       char[4] "GGUF"
    version     u32     "format version, 3 for current files"
    tensorCount u64     "number of tensors"
    kvCount     u64     "number of metadata key/value pairs"
    metadata    GgufKv[kvCount]              "model metadata: architecture, hyperparameters, tokenizer"
    tensors     GgufTensorInfo[tensorCount]  "tensor directory; the data follows, aligned"
}

formats.name: HDF5
formats.description: Hierarchical Data Format 5, superblock versions 0 to 3
formats.schema:
// HDF5 - the Hierarchical Data Format, a filesystem in a file for scientific
// and numeric data. Groups hold named links to other groups and to datasets,
// and every object is described by an object header: a list of typed messages
// (dataspace, datatype, layout, attributes). NetCDF-4, MATLAB v7.3 .mat files
// and Keras .h5 models are all HDF5 underneath.
//
// The superblock is usually at offset 0 (it may also sit at 512, 1024, 2048...
// behind a user block). Versions 0 and 1 reach the root group through a symbol
// table entry whose scratch space points straight at the group's B-tree and
// local name heap; versions 2 and 3 point at the root's object header and keep
// group links inside it.
//
// Addresses are read as 64-bit and taken as file offsets: this assumes the
// near-universal 8-byte "size of offsets" and a base address of 0. An address
// of all ones (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) means "undefined".

enum HdfMessageType : u16 {
    Nil                 = 0
    Dataspace           = 1
    LinkInfo            = 2
    Datatype            = 3
    FillValueOld        = 4
    FillValue           = 5
    Link                = 6
    ExternalFiles       = 7
    DataLayout          = 8
    Bogus               = 9
    GroupInfo           = 10
    FilterPipeline      = 11
    Attribute           = 12
    ObjectComment       = 13
    ModificationTimeOld = 14
    SharedMessageTable  = 15
    Continuation        = 16
    SymbolTable         = 17
    ModificationTime    = 18
    BtreeKValues        = 19
    DriverInfo          = 20
    AttributeInfo       = 21
    ReferenceCount      = 22
    FileSpaceInfo       = 23
}

// The same message types, stored in one byte by version 2 object headers.
enum HdfMessageTypeV2 : u8 {
    Nil                 = 0
    Dataspace           = 1
    LinkInfo            = 2
    Datatype            = 3
    FillValueOld        = 4
    FillValue           = 5
    Link                = 6
    ExternalFiles       = 7
    DataLayout          = 8
    Bogus               = 9
    GroupInfo           = 10
    FilterPipeline      = 11
    Attribute           = 12
    ObjectComment       = 13
    ModificationTimeOld = 14
    SharedMessageTable  = 15
    Continuation        = 16
    SymbolTable         = 17
    ModificationTime    = 18
    BtreeKValues        = 19
    DriverInfo          = 20
    AttributeInfo       = 21
    ReferenceCount      = 22
    FileSpaceInfo       = 23
}

bitfield HdfConsistencyFlags : u32 {
    writeAccess 0 // a writer has the file open
    swmrWrite   2 // opened for single-writer / multiple-reader access
}

bitfield HdfObjectHeaderFlags : u8 {
    chunkSizeWidth     0..1 // width of the chunk 0 size: 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes
    trackCreationOrder 2    // attribute creation order is tracked
    indexCreationOrder 3    // attribute creation order is indexed
    storePhaseChange   4    // non-default attribute storage thresholds follow
    storeTimes         5    // access, modification, change and birth times follow
}

struct HdfMessageV1 {
    type     HdfMessageType "what the message describes"
    size     u16            "bytes of message data"
    flags    u8             "bit 0 constant, bit 1 shared, bit 3 fail if not understood"
    reserved bytes[3]
    data     bytes[size]
}

// Version 1 object header, the only kind version 0/1 superblocks write. The
// message count includes messages in continuation blocks elsewhere in the
// file, so only the first message of this block is decoded.
struct HdfObjectHeaderV1 {
    version      u8           "1"
    reserved     u8
    numMessages  u16          "messages in this header, across all of its blocks"
    refCount     u32          "number of hard links to this object"
    headerSize   u32          "bytes of messages in this first block"
    padding      u32          "aligns the messages to 8 bytes"
    firstMessage HdfMessageV1 "first header message"
}

// Version 2 object header ("OHDR"), written under version 2 and 3 superblocks.
// Messages run to the end of chunk 0; only the first is decoded.
struct HdfObjectHeaderV2 {
    signature            char[4] "OHDR"
    version              u8      "2"
    flags                HdfObjectHeaderFlags
    accessTime           u32 if flags.storeTimes "unix time"
    modificationTime     u32 if flags.storeTimes "unix time"
    changeTime           u32 if flags.storeTimes "unix time"
    birthTime            u32 if flags.storeTimes "unix time"
    maxCompactAttributes u16 if flags.storePhaseChange "attributes kept in the header before moving to dense storage"
    minDenseAttributes   u16 if flags.storePhaseChange "attribute count below which dense storage moves back"
    chunkSize match flags.chunkSizeWidth {
        0 => u8
        1 => u16
        2 => u32
        3 => u64
    }
    firstType          HdfMessageTypeV2 "first header message: type"
    firstSize          u16              "first header message: bytes of data"
    firstFlags         u8               "first header message: flags"
    firstCreationOrder u16 if flags.trackCreationOrder
    firstData          bytes[firstSize] "first header message: data"
}

// Local heap: the names of a group's members, as NUL-terminated strings.
struct HdfLocalHeap {
    signature          char[4]  "HEAP"
    version            u8
    reserved           bytes[3]
    dataSegmentSize    u64      "bytes in the data segment"
    freeListOffset     u64      "offset of the first free block, or undefined"
    dataSegmentAddress u64      "address of the data segment"
    names at dataSegmentAddress bytes[dataSegmentSize] "member names, NUL-terminated and 8-byte padded"
}

// Symbol table node: one leaf of a group's B-tree, a run of entries.
struct HdfSymbolNode {
    signature  char[4] "SNOD"
    version    u8      "1"
    reserved   u8
    numSymbols u16     "entries in use in this node"
    entries    HdfSymbolTableEntry[numSymbols] "group members; each name is an offset into the local heap"
}

// One child of a group B-tree node. The child's signature says what it is: a
// symbol table node at the leaves, another B-tree node above them.
struct HdfGroupBtreeEntry {
    child          u64 "address of the child node"
    key            u64 "heap offset of the largest name under that child"
    childSignature at child char[4]
    node at child match childSignature {
        "SNOD"  => HdfSymbolNode
        "TREE"  => HdfBtreeV1
        default => bytes[0]
    }
}

// Version 1 B-tree node. Type 0 indexes a group's members by name; type 1
// indexes a chunked dataset's chunks and has wider keys, left undecoded here.
struct HdfBtreeV1 {
    signature    char[4] "TREE"
    nodeType     u8      "0 group members, 1 raw data chunks"
    nodeLevel    u8      "0 for a leaf"
    entriesUsed  u16     "children in this node"
    leftSibling  u64     "address of the left sibling, or undefined"
    rightSibling u64     "address of the right sibling, or undefined"
    firstKey     u64     if nodeType == 0 "heap offset of the empty name"
    entries      HdfGroupBtreeEntry[entriesUsed] if nodeType == 0
}

// A symbol table entry: one name in a group, pointing at the named object.
// With cache type 1 the object is itself a group, and the scratch space holds
// the addresses of its B-tree and name heap.
struct HdfSymbolTableEntry {
    linkNameOffset      u64 "offset of this entry's name in the parent's local heap"
    objectHeaderAddress u64 "address of the object's header"
    cacheType           u32 "0 nothing cached, 1 group B-tree and heap addresses, 2 symbolic link"
    reserved            u32
    btreeAddress        u64       if cacheType == 1 "address of the group's B-tree"
    heapAddress         u64       if cacheType == 1 "address of the group's local heap"
    scratch             bytes[16] if cacheType != 1
    objectHeader at objectHeaderAddress HdfObjectHeaderV1 "the object's header"
    btree at btreeAddress HdfBtreeV1   if cacheType == 1 "the group's member index"
    heap  at heapAddress  HdfLocalHeap if cacheType == 1 "the group's member names"
}

struct HdfSuperblockV0 {
    freeSpaceVersion       u8  "0"
    rootSymbolTableVersion u8  "0"
    reserved0              u8
    sharedHeaderVersion    u8  "0"
    sizeOfOffsets          u8  "bytes per address, almost always 8"
    sizeOfLengths          u8  "bytes per length, almost always 8"
    reserved1              u8
    groupLeafNodeK         u16 "half the maximum entries in a symbol table node"
    groupInternalNodeK     u16 "half the maximum children of a group B-tree node"
    consistencyFlags       HdfConsistencyFlags
    baseAddress            u64 "addresses are relative to this, usually 0"
    freeSpaceAddress       u64 "free-space info, undefined in practice"
    endOfFileAddress       u64 "end of the file's allocated space"
    driverInfoAddress      u64 "driver information block, or undefined"
    rootGroup              HdfSymbolTableEntry "the root group"
}

// Version 1 adds the chunk B-tree K after the consistency flags.
struct HdfSuperblockV1 {
    freeSpaceVersion       u8  "0"
    rootSymbolTableVersion u8  "0"
    reserved0              u8
    sharedHeaderVersion    u8  "0"
    sizeOfOffsets          u8  "bytes per address, almost always 8"
    sizeOfLengths          u8  "bytes per length, almost always 8"
    reserved1              u8
    groupLeafNodeK         u16 "half the maximum entries in a symbol table node"
    groupInternalNodeK     u16 "half the maximum children of a group B-tree node"
    consistencyFlags       HdfConsistencyFlags
    indexedStorageK        u16 "half the maximum children of a chunk B-tree node"
    reserved2              u16
    baseAddress            u64 "addresses are relative to this, usually 0"
    freeSpaceAddress       u64 "free-space info, undefined in practice"
    endOfFileAddress       u64 "end of the file's allocated space"
    driverInfoAddress      u64 "driver information block, or undefined"
    rootGroup              HdfSymbolTableEntry "the root group"
}

struct HdfSuperblockV2 {
    sizeOfOffsets           u8  "bytes per address, almost always 8"
    sizeOfLengths           u8  "bytes per length, almost always 8"
    consistencyFlags        u8  "bit 0 write access, bit 2 SWMR write"
    baseAddress             u64 "addresses are relative to this, usually 0"
    extensionAddress        u64 "superblock extension object header, or undefined"
    endOfFileAddress        u64 "end of the file's allocated space"
    rootObjectHeaderAddress u64 "address of the root group's object header"
    checksum                u32 "Jenkins lookup3 hash of the superblock"
    rootObjectHeader at rootObjectHeaderAddress HdfObjectHeaderV2 "the root group"
}

struct Hdf5 {
    signature bytes[8] "89 HDF CR LF 1A LF, a PNG-style signature"
    version   u8       "superblock version: 0, 1, 2 or 3"
    superblock match version {
        0 => HdfSuperblockV0
        1 => HdfSuperblockV1
        2 => HdfSuperblockV2
        3 => HdfSuperblockV2
    }
}

formats.name: ISO9660
formats.schema:
// ISO 9660 - the CD-ROM filesystem, and still what a .iso file is. The first
// sixteen 2048-byte sectors are the system area, reserved for whatever the
// platform needs to boot; the filesystem proper starts at 32768 with a chain
// of volume descriptors, terminated by one of type 255.
//
// Its defining quirk is that every multi-byte number is stored twice, once
// little-endian and once big-endian, back to back, so a reader of either byte
// order could use the disc without swapping. The pairs are shown here as two
// fields; the two halves always agree.
//
// Dates come in two shapes: a 17-character ASCII form for the volume, down to
// hundredths of a second, and a packed 7-byte form for directory entries.

bitfield IsoFileFlags : u8 {
    hidden      0 // hide this entry from the user
    directory   1 // this entry is a directory
    associated  2 // an associated file (a resource fork)
    record      3 // the extended attribute record has record information
    protection  4 // permissions are recorded in the extended attributes
    multiExtent 7 // this is not the final extent of the file
}

// A directory record. 33 fixed bytes plus the name, padded to an even length.
struct IsoDirectoryRecord {
    length         u8           "length of this record, name and padding included"
    extAttrLength  u8           "length of the extended attribute record, in sectors"
    extentLe       u32          "first sector of the file contents"
    extentBe       u32          "the same, big-endian"
    dataLengthLe   u32          "size of the file in bytes"
    dataLengthBe   u32          "the same, big-endian"
    recordingDate  bytes[7]     "year since 1900, month, day, hour, minute, second, GMT offset"
    flags          IsoFileFlags "directory, hidden, multi-extent, ..."
    fileUnitSize   u8           "file unit size, for interleaved files"
    interleaveGap  u8           "interleave gap size"
    volumeSeqLe    u16          "volume in the set holding this file"
    volumeSeqBe    u16          "the same, big-endian"
    nameLength     u8           "length of the identifier that follows"
    name           char[nameLength] "file name; 0x00 is . and 0x01 is .."
}

// The primary volume descriptor: what a reader needs to mount the disc.
struct IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor {
    type              u8       "1 for the primary volume descriptor"
    identifier        char[5]  "CD001"
    version           u8       "1"
    unused            u8       "zero"
    systemId          char[32] "system that can act on the first 16 sectors"
    volumeId          char[32] "volume label"
    unused2           bytes[8] "zero"
    volumeSpaceSizeLe u32      "sectors on the volume"
    volumeSpaceSizeBe u32      "the same, big-endian"
    unused3           bytes[32] "zero"
    volumeSetSizeLe   u16      "discs in the set"
    volumeSetSizeBe   u16      "the same, big-endian"
    volumeSeqLe       u16      "position of this disc in the set"
    volumeSeqBe       u16      "the same, big-endian"
    logicalBlockSizeLe u16     "sector size, effectively always 2048"
    logicalBlockSizeBe u16     "the same, big-endian"
    pathTableSizeLe   u32      "size of the path table in bytes"
    pathTableSizeBe   u32      "the same, big-endian"
    typeLPathTable    u32      "sector of the little-endian path table"
    optTypeLPathTable u32      "sector of its optional copy, 0 if there is none"
    typeMPathTable    u32      "sector of the big-endian path table (a big-endian value)"
    optTypeMPathTable u32      "sector of its optional copy"
    rootDirectory     IsoDirectoryRecord "the root directory record, always 34 bytes here"
    volumeSetId       char[128] "name of the multi-disc set"
    publisherId       char[128] "publisher"
    dataPreparerId    char[128] "who prepared the data"
    applicationId     char[128] "application that wrote the disc"
    copyrightFileId   char[37]  "file in the root holding the copyright notice"
    abstractFileId    char[37]  "file in the root holding the abstract"
    bibliographicFileId char[37] "file in the root holding the bibliography"
    creationDate      char[17]  "YYYYMMDDHHMMSSCC plus a GMT offset byte"
    modificationDate  char[17]  "last modification"
    expirationDate    char[17]  "after which the volume is obsolete"
    effectiveDate     char[17]  "before which the volume should not be used"
    fileStructureVersion u8     "1"
    unused4           u8        "zero"
    applicationUse    bytes[512] "free for the application that wrote the disc"
    reserved          bytes[653] "reserved, zero"
}

struct Iso9660 {
    systemArea bytes[32768] "sectors 0-15: boot sectors and partition maps, not ISO 9660"
    pvd        IsoPrimaryVolumeDescriptor "the primary volume descriptor, at sector 16"
}

packs.description: NIfTI-1 348-byte header: dimensions, data type, scaling and both spatial transforms.
packs.author: Nybble

formats.name: NIfTI
formats.schema:
// NIfTI-1 - the neuroimaging volume format, and a careful extension of the
// older ANALYZE 7.5 header it is binary-compatible with. The header is exactly
// 348 bytes; in a .nii file the voxels follow at voxOffset (352 when there are
// no extensions, because a 4-byte extension flag sits after the header).
//
// Several fields exist only to keep ANALYZE readers working - dataType,
// dbName, extents, regular and the glmax / glmin pair are unused by NIfTI and
// are documented as such below.
//
// What makes the format worth reading is that it records where the voxels are
// in the scanner, not just how many there are. Two independent transforms map
// voxel indices to millimetres in a right-handed anatomical space: a rigid one
// stored as a quaternion (qform, the scanner's own position) and a full affine
// stored as three rows (sform, usually the result of registering to a template).
// Either may be unused; qformCode and sformCode say which to trust.
//
// dim is index-based: dim[0] is how many of the remaining entries are in use,
// then dim[1..3] are the spatial sizes, dim[4] the time points, and dim[5..7]
// any further dimensions. pixdim matches it, with pixdim[0] carrying the sign
// of the qform determinant rather than a size.

enum NiftiDataType : i16 {
    Unknown    = 0
    Binary     = 1   // 1 bit per voxel
    Uint8      = 2
    Int16      = 4
    Int32      = 8
    Float32    = 16
    Complex64  = 32  // two 32-bit floats
    Float64    = 64
    Rgb24      = 128 // three bytes per voxel
    Int8       = 256
    Uint16     = 512
    Uint32     = 768
    Int64      = 1024
    Uint64     = 1280
    Float128   = 1536
    Complex128 = 1792 // two 64-bit floats
    Complex256 = 2048
    Rgba32     = 2304
}

enum NiftiIntent : i16 {
    None          = 0
    Correlation   = 2
    TTest         = 3
    FTest         = 4
    ZScore        = 5
    ChiSquared    = 6
    Beta          = 7
    Pval          = 22
    LogPval       = 23
    Estimate      = 1001 // the values are parameter estimates, not statistics
    Label         = 1002 // an atlas or segmentation: each value names a region
    Neuroname     = 1003
    GeneralMatrix = 1004
    SymmetricMatrix = 1005
    DisplacementVector = 1006
    Vector        = 1007
    Pointset      = 1008
    Triangle      = 1009
    Quaternion    = 1010
    Dimensionless = 1011
}

enum NiftiXform : i16 {
    Unknown      = 0 // this transform is unused; fall back to pixdim scaling
    ScannerAnat  = 1 // scanner-based anatomical coordinates
    AlignedAnat  = 2 // aligned to another image in the same session
    Talairach    = 3 // Talairach-Tournoux atlas space
    Mni152       = 4 // MNI 152 template space
}

enum NiftiSliceCode : u8 {
    Unknown         = 0
    Sequential      = 1 // 1, 2, 3, ... in increasing z
    SequentialDown  = 2 // in decreasing z
    Alternating     = 3 // interleaved, starting at the first slice
    AlternatingDown = 4
    Alternating2    = 5 // interleaved, starting at the second slice
    Alternating2Down = 6
}

// xyztUnits packs two unit codes into one byte: the low three bits are the
// spatial unit, the next three the temporal one. 1 metre, 2 millimetre,
// 3 micrometre; 8 second, 16 millisecond, 24 microsecond, and 32, 40, 48 for
// the frequency-domain units Hz, ppm and rad/s.
bitfield NiftiUnits : u8 {
    space 0..2
    time  3..5
}

struct Nifti1 {
    sizeofHdr    i32           "header size; must be 348"
    dataType     string[10]    "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    dbName       string[18]    "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    extents      i32           "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    sessionError i16           "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    regular      char          "unused; ANALYZE writers put r here"
    dimInfo      u8            "which dimension is frequency, phase and slice encoded, 2 bits each"
    dim          i16[8]        "dim[0] is the number of dimensions in use; dim[1..3] the volume size, dim[4] time points"
    intentP1     f32           "first intent parameter, meaning set by intentCode"
    intentP2     f32           "second intent parameter"
    intentP3     f32           "third intent parameter"
    intentCode   NiftiIntent   "what the voxel values mean"
    datatype     NiftiDataType "how each voxel is stored"
    bitpix       i16           "bits per voxel; must agree with datatype"
    sliceStart   i16           "index of the first slice acquired"
    pixdim       f32[8]        "voxel size along each dimension; pixdim[0] carries the qform determinant sign"
    voxOffset    f32           "file offset of the voxel data; 352 in a .nii with no extensions"
    sclSlope     f32           "scaling: real value = sclSlope * stored + sclInter (0 means no scaling)"
    sclInter     f32           "scaling intercept"
    sliceEnd     i16           "index of the last slice acquired"
    sliceCode    NiftiSliceCode "slice timing order"
    xyztUnits    NiftiUnits    "units for the spatial and temporal dimensions"
    calMax       f32           "display window maximum"
    calMin       f32           "display window minimum"
    sliceDuration f32          "time to acquire one slice"
    toffset      f32           "time of the first volume, in the temporal unit"
    glmax        i32           "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    glmin        i32           "unused, kept for ANALYZE compatibility"
    descrip      string[80]    "free-form description, often the scanner and sequence"
    auxFile      string[24]    "name of an auxiliary file"
    qformCode    NiftiXform    "space the quaternion transform maps into; 0 means unused"
    sformCode    NiftiXform    "space the affine transform maps into; 0 means unused"
    quaternB     f32           "quaternion i component; the real part is derived from the three"
    quaternC     f32           "quaternion j component"
    quaternD     f32           "quaternion k component"
    qoffsetX     f32           "translation, x (mm)"
    qoffsetY     f32           "translation, y (mm)"
    qoffsetZ     f32           "translation, z (mm)"
    srowX        f32[4]        "first row of the affine transform"
    srowY        f32[4]        "second row of the affine transform"
    srowZ        f32[4]        "third row of the affine transform"
    intentName   string[16]    "name or meaning of the data, when intentCode needs one"
    magic        string[4]     "n+1 for a single .nii file, ni1 for a .hdr / .img pair"
}

formats.name: PE
formats.description: Windows portable executable (exe, dll, sys, ocx)
formats.schema:
// PE - the Windows executable. It still opens with a DOS MZ header, kept so a
// 1990 DOS box could print "This program cannot be run in DOS mode". The only
// field of it that matters today is e_lfanew, the offset of the real PE header,
// which is followed here by pointer.
//
// After the PE signature come the COFF header (machine, section count, the
// characteristics that say exe or dll) and the optional header, which is not
// optional for an image: it holds the entry point, the image base, the
// subsystem, and the data directories the loader uses to find the imports,
// exports, relocations and certificates. PE32 and PE32+ differ only in a
// handful of fields that widen to 64 bits, guarded below by the magic.

enum PeMachine : u16 {
    Unknown   = 0x0000
    I386      = 0x014C
    R4000Mips = 0x0166
    Sh3       = 0x01A2
    Sh4       = 0x01A6
    Arm       = 0x01C0
    Thumb     = 0x01C2
    ArmNt     = 0x01C4
    PowerPc   = 0x01F0
    Ia64      = 0x0200
    MipsFpu   = 0x0366
    Ebc       = 0x0EBC
    Amd64     = 0x8664
    Arm64     = 0xAA64
    RiscV32   = 0x5032
    RiscV64   = 0x5064
    RiscV128  = 0x5128
}

bitfield PeCharacteristics : u16 {
    relocsStripped       0
    executableImage      1
    lineNumsStripped     2
    localSymsStripped    3
    aggressiveWsTrim     4
    largeAddressAware    5  // can use more than 2 GB of address space
    bytesReversedLo      7
    machine32Bit         8
    debugStripped        9
    removableRunFromSwap 10
    netRunFromSwap       11
    system               12
    dll                  13 // a DLL rather than an executable
    upSystemOnly         14
    bytesReversedHi      15
}

enum PeSubsystem : u16 {
    Unknown                = 0
    Native                 = 1
    WindowsGui             = 2
    WindowsCui             = 3
    Os2Cui                 = 5
    PosixCui               = 7
    NativeWindows          = 8
    WindowsCeGui           = 9
    EfiApplication         = 10
    EfiBootServiceDriver   = 11
    EfiRuntimeDriver       = 12
    EfiRom                 = 13
    Xbox                   = 14
    WindowsBootApplication = 16
}

bitfield PeDllCharacteristics : u16 {
    highEntropyVa       5  // 64-bit ASLR with a full-width address space
    dynamicBase         6  // ASLR: the image can be relocated at load
    forceIntegrity      7
    nxCompat            8  // DEP: data pages are not executable
    noIsolation         9
    noSeh               10
    noBind              11
    appContainer        12
    wdmDriver           13
    guardCf             14 // Control Flow Guard
    terminalServerAware 15
}

bitfield PeSectionFlags : u32 {
    code               5
    initializedData    6
    uninitializedData  7  // .bss: occupies memory but no file bytes
    linkInfo           9
    linkRemove         11
    linkComdat         12
    gprel              15
    alignMask          20..23 // alignment is 2^(n-1) bytes
    linkNrelocOvfl     24
    memDiscardable     25
    memNotCached       26
    memNotPaged        27
    memShared          28
    memExecute         29
    memRead            30
    memWrite           31
}

// The DOS header. Everything but lfanew is vestigial.
struct PeDosHeader {
    magic     char[2]  "MZ, for Mark Zbikowski"
    cblp      u16      "bytes on the last page of the DOS image"
    cp        u16      "pages in the DOS image"
    crlc      u16      "relocation entries"
    cparhdr   u16      "header size in 16-byte paragraphs"
    minalloc  u16      "minimum extra paragraphs needed"
    maxalloc  u16      "maximum extra paragraphs needed"
    ss        u16      "initial SS, relative to the load segment"
    sp        u16      "initial SP"
    csum      u16      "checksum, normally left zero"
    ip        u16      "initial IP"
    cs        u16      "initial CS, relative to the load segment"
    lfarlc    u16      "file offset of the relocation table"
    ovno      u16      "overlay number"
    reserved  bytes[8] "reserved words"
    oemid     u16      "OEM identifier"
    oeminfo   u16      "OEM information"
    reserved2 bytes[20] "reserved words"
    lfanew    u32      "file offset of the PE signature: the only field that still matters"
}

// One data directory entry: an RVA and a size, or two zeros when absent.
struct PeDataDirectory {
    virtualAddress u32 "RVA of the table, 0 when the entry is unused"
    size           u32 "size of the table in bytes"
}

struct PeOptionalHeader {
    magic                   u16 "0x10B = PE32, 0x20B = PE32+, 0x107 = ROM image"
    majorLinkerVersion      u8
    minorLinkerVersion      u8
    sizeOfCode              u32 "total size of the code sections"
    sizeOfInitializedData   u32 "total size of the initialized data sections"
    sizeOfUninitializedData u32 "total size of the .bss sections"
    addressOfEntryPoint     u32 "RVA of the entry point; 0 for a DLL with no entry"
    baseOfCode              u32 "RVA of the start of the code"
    baseOfData              u32 if magic == 0x10B "RVA of the start of the data; PE32 only"
    imageBase32             u32 if magic == 0x10B "preferred load address"
    imageBase64             u64 if magic == 0x20B "preferred load address"
    sectionAlignment        u32 "section alignment in memory"
    fileAlignment           u32 "section alignment in the file, usually 512"
    majorOsVersion          u16
    minorOsVersion          u16
    majorImageVersion       u16
    minorImageVersion       u16
    majorSubsystemVersion   u16
    minorSubsystemVersion   u16
    win32VersionValue       u32 "reserved, zero"
    sizeOfImage             u32 "size of the loaded image, rounded to sectionAlignment"
    sizeOfHeaders           u32 "headers plus the section table, rounded to fileAlignment"
    checkSum                u32 "image checksum; required for drivers and system DLLs"
    subsystem               PeSubsystem          "what runs this image"
    dllCharacteristics      PeDllCharacteristics "ASLR, DEP, CFG and friends"
    sizeOfStackReserve32    u32 if magic == 0x10B "virtual address space reserved for the stack"
    sizeOfStackCommit32     u32 if magic == 0x10B "stack committed up front"
    sizeOfHeapReserve32     u32 if magic == 0x10B "address space reserved for the default heap"
    sizeOfHeapCommit32      u32 if magic == 0x10B "heap committed up front"
    sizeOfStackReserve64    u64 if magic == 0x20B "virtual address space reserved for the stack"
    sizeOfStackCommit64     u64 if magic == 0x20B "stack committed up front"
    sizeOfHeapReserve64     u64 if magic == 0x20B "address space reserved for the default heap"
    sizeOfHeapCommit64      u64 if magic == 0x20B "heap committed up front"
    loaderFlags             u32 "reserved, zero"
    numberOfRvaAndSizes     u32 "data directory entries that follow, normally 16"
    // In order: export, import, resource, exception, certificate, base
    // relocation, debug, architecture, global pointer, TLS, load config,
    // bound import, IAT, delay import, CLR runtime header, reserved.
    dataDirectories PeDataDirectory[numberOfRvaAndSizes] "where the loader finds each table"
}

struct PeSection {
    name                 char[8]        "section name, NUL-padded, not NUL-terminated"
    virtualSize          u32            "size of the section once loaded"
    virtualAddress       u32            "RVA of the section in the loaded image"
    sizeOfRawData        u32            "bytes in the file, rounded to fileAlignment"
    pointerToRawData     u32            "file offset of the section contents"
    pointerToRelocations u32            "file offset of the relocations, object files only"
    pointerToLinenumbers u32            "deprecated, zero"
    numberOfRelocations  u16            "object files only"
    numberOfLinenumbers  u16            "deprecated, zero"
    characteristics      PeSectionFlags "contents and the page protection to map it with"
}

struct PeHeader {
    signature            bytes[4]           "50 45 00 00, the PE signature"
    machine              PeMachine          "target architecture"
    numberOfSections     u16                "entries in the section table"
    timeDateStamp        u32                "link time (unix); often a reproducible-build hash"
    pointerToSymbolTable u32                "COFF symbol table offset, 0 in an image"
    numberOfSymbols      u32                "COFF symbols, 0 in an image"
    sizeOfOptionalHeader u16                "bytes of optional header that follow"
    characteristics      PeCharacteristics  "exe or dll, and how it may be loaded"
    optional             PeOptionalHeader   "entry point, image base, subsystem, directories"
    sections             PeSection[numberOfSections] "the section table"
}

struct Pe {
    dos  PeDosHeader "the DOS stub header"
    // The PE header, reached through e_lfanew. Placed by pointer, so the DOS
    // stub code between the two is left where it is.
    pe at dos.lfanew PeHeader "the PE header the Windows loader actually reads"
}

formats.name: RAR5
RAR4
formats.schema:
// RAR 1.5 - 4.x — a 7-byte signature, then blocks: CRC-16, type, flags, header
// size, and (when bit 15 of the flags is set) a 32-bit size of data that
// follows the header. That makes every block walkable, so this pack lists all
// of them and decodes the main and file headers by pointer.

enum Rar4BlockType : u8 {
    Marker      = 0x72
    Main        = 0x73
    File        = 0x74
    Comment     = 0x75
    ExtraInfo   = 0x76
    Subblock    = 0x77
    Recovery    = 0x78
    AuthInfo    = 0x79
    NewSubblock = 0x7A
    EndArchive  = 0x7B
}

bitfield Rar4BlockFlags : u16 {
    skipIfUnknown 14 // block may be skipped if its type is unknown
    longBlock     15 // a 32-bit data size follows the header size
}

bitfield Rar4MainFlags : u16 {
    volume            0  // multi-volume archive
    comment           1  // an (old style) comment block follows
    locked            2  // archive is locked
    solid             3  // solid archive
    newNumbering      4  // new volume naming scheme
    authInfo          5  // authenticity information present
    recovery          6  // recovery record present
    passwordEncrypted 7  // headers are encrypted
    firstVolume       8  // this is the first volume
    encryptVer        9  // encryption version field present
    longBlock         15
}

bitfield Rar4FileFlags : u16 {
    splitBefore 0    // continued from the previous volume
    splitAfter  1    // continues in the next volume
    password    2    // file is encrypted
    comment     3    // a file comment follows
    solid       4    // uses data from previous files
    dictionary  5..7 // dictionary size: 0 = 64K .. 6 = 4096K, 7 = directory
    largeFile   8    // 64-bit sizes: high 32 bits follow
    unicode     9    // file name contains a Unicode variant
    salt        10   // an 8-byte salt follows
    version     11   // file versioning
    extTime     12   // extended time fields follow
    longBlock   15
}

enum Rar4HostOs : u8 {
    MsDos = 0
    Os2   = 1
    Win32 = 2
    Unix  = 3
    MacOs = 4
    BeOs  = 5
}

enum Rar4Method : u8 {
    Store   = 0x30
    Fastest = 0x31
    Fast    = 0x32
    Normal  = 0x33
    Good    = 0x34
    Best    = 0x35
}

struct Rar4MainHeader {
    crc       u16           "CRC-16 of the header"
    type      Rar4BlockType "0x73"
    flags     Rar4MainFlags "archive flags"
    headSize  u16           "header size (13)"
    reserved1 u16
    reserved2 u32
}

struct Rar4FileHeader {
    crc          u16           "CRC-16 of the header"
    type         Rar4BlockType "0x74"
    flags        Rar4FileFlags "file flags"
    headSize     u16           "header size including the file name"
    packSize     u32           "packed size (low 32 bits)"
    unpSize      u32           "unpacked size (low 32 bits)"
    hostOs       Rar4HostOs    "OS the file was archived on"
    fileCrc      u32           "CRC-32 of the unpacked file"
    fileTime     u32           "modification time (MS-DOS date/time)"
    unpVer       u8            "RAR version needed to extract (x10: 29 = 2.9)"
    method       Rar4Method    "compression method"
    nameSize     u16           "file name length"
    attr         u32           "file attributes (host OS specific)"
    highPackSize u32           if flags.largeFile "high 32 bits of the packed size"
    highUnpSize  u32           if flags.largeFile "high 32 bits of the unpacked size"
    fileName     string[nameSize] "file name"
    salt         bytes[8]      if flags.salt "encryption salt"
}

struct Rar4Block {
    crc      u16            "CRC-16 of the header"
    type     Rar4BlockType  "block type"
    flags    Rar4BlockFlags "block flags (bit 15: data follows)"
    headSize u16            "header size, this field included"
    addSize  u32            if flags.longBlock "size of the data after the header"
    // Remaining header bytes: 7 fixed bytes so far, plus 4 more if addSize is present.
    restShort   = headSize - 7
    restLong    = headSize - 11
    headerRest  bytes[restShort] if flags.longBlock == 0 "rest of the header"
    headerRest2 bytes[restLong]  if flags.longBlock      "rest of the header"
    data        bytes[addSize]   if flags.longBlock      "block data (packed file contents)"
    // Typed view of the whole header, by pointer, for the block types that matter.
    decoded at +0 match type {
        0x73    => Rar4MainHeader
        0x74    => Rar4FileHeader
        default => bytes[0]
    }
}

struct Rar4 {
    signature bytes[7] "52 61 72 21 1A 07 00"
    blocks repeat Rar4Block until type == 0x7B "every block, up to the end-of-archive block"
}
